summary: Douglas County, OR lookout on the Umpqua NF, built 1933 as an L-5 cab and removed or destroyed in 1963; no source found that describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Cab removed in 1963 per the register and Forest Lookouts; firelookout.com says destroyed; no source describes remains at the site

events.note: L-5 cab at the southwest end of the summit ridge, per the register and firelookout.com
Roseburg Chieftain item dated September 14, 1933, quoted on the Forest Lookouts page: a 10 x 10 lookout to be built by the CCC before the snow flies
Panorama photos taken August 20, 1933, by Cooper and Sarlin
New set of panorama photos taken August 2 and 3, 1936, by Rittenhouse
Register and Forest Lookouts say removed; firelookout.com says destroyed
Registered March 28, 2011, nominated by Ray Kresek

evidence.supports: built 1933 at the southwest end of the summit ridge as an L-5 cab; removed 1963
evidence.quote: Built in 1933 at the extreme southwest end of the long summit ridge, this L-5 cab was removed in 1963.

evidence.supports: site in the Umpqua National Forest, Douglas County
1933 plan for a 10 x 10 lookout to be built by the CCC
evidence.quote: A 10 x 10 lookout is to be built by the CCC before the snow flies.

evidence.supports: panorama photos taken August 20, 1933 by Cooper and Sarlin
evidence.quote: August 20, 1933: Panorama photos were taken by Cooper and Sarlin.

evidence.supports: new panorama photos August 2 and 3, 1936 by Rittenhouse
evidence.quote: August 2 & 3, 1936: A new set of panorama photos were taken by Rittenhouse.

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts page lists the lookout as removed, with no date

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The September 1933 newspaper item describes a planned 10 x 10 lookout, while the register describes a built L-5 cab. The sources do not say whether these are the same structure, so the story reports both without equating them.

notes_for_editor: Search results included a Montana lookout also called Reynolds Ridge (mtmemory.org; firelookout.com/mt), built 1931 and destroyed 1962. It is a different lookout and was not used. The fate disagreement (removed versus destroyed, both 1963) is reported as a disagreement. No staffing or fire history was found in the sources read; the story leaves those out.
